extracted.intended_audience: university administrators, comptrollers, grants and contracts officers, research administrators, and faculty governance (presidents, faculty senates) involved in federal research accounting
extracted.subtask_short: effort reporting under OMB Circular A-21
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for designing, negotiating, and implementing faculty effort reporting and alternative accountability systems under OMB Circular A-21, including examples from Stanford and Yale and recommended practices for documenting indirect costs of research.

rubrics_metrics.name: 100 percent effort reporting requirement (1979 A-21)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 1979 revision required faculty to account for 100 percent of the time for which they were compensated, reflecting the ratio of each activity comprising the total workload.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement called for allocation of all salaried activities into workload categories applicable to sponsored agreements and indirect cost activities. The workshop identifies this as burdensome and often unworkable in an academic setting because faculty activities are intermingled (research, teaching, service). Anti-pattern: insisting on precise, project-by-project percentages for every faculty member.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report effort by discrete categories and percentages
rubrics_metrics.description: Effort reporting systems call on faculty members to allot their time among discrete functions (teaching, research, service, administration) and express them as percentages of total effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Circular A-21 recognizes that activities are often inextricably intermingled and allows approximations, but in practice the categorical percent reporting is applied rigidly. The report warns that forcing discrete separation can create spurious categories and meaningless reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of reasonably accurate approximations and tolerance
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB Circular A-21 acknowledges that various interrelated activities cannot be measured with high precision and calls for reliance on reasonably accurate approximations and acceptance of a degree of tolerance in measurement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although A-21 allows approximations, many institutions and auditors lack confidence in their effectiveness. Guidance: institutions should document rationale for approximations and tolerance levels to withstand audit scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personnel Activity Reporting (PAR) form requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of Personnel Activity Reporting forms (PAR) where employees (faculty and certain professional staff) estimate distribution of effort for a reporting period and certify the distribution; total should equal 100%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples (Appendix III) show PAR forms with category checklists (instructional research, sponsored research, department administration, etc.), instructions, and certification signatures. Anti-pattern: relying on PARs to force artificial separations of activities; ensure forms and instructions recognize intermingled activities and permit reasonable estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitored Workload System as an alternative method
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitored Workload System is an A-21-sanctioned alternative to PAR for documenting work effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 1979 A-21 contained Personnel Activity Reporting and Monitored Workload as alternatives; the 1982 revision expanded acceptable alternatives. Institutions may choose the system that best fits their operations and document its validity for auditors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stipulated salary support method
rubrics_metrics.description: A method for reporting direct costs in which stipulated salary support is determined by judgment of monetary value of expected contribution to a research project for certain professional staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires documentation on total salary, other research projects, planned participation, institutional duties, summer salaries, handling changes, and audit provisions. Use only where appropriate and with clear supporting records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payroll distribution method
rubrics_metrics.description: A method for reporting direct costs based on the institution's payroll system, supported by appointment and work records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires institution payroll records or timekeeping documentation that qualify as adequate support under A-21. Ensure payroll records meet the specified documentation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of direct charges by investigators
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators must certify that salary and wage charges to sponsored projects have been reviewed and are reasonably accurate approximations of effort applied and charged to the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stanford and Yale use concise certification statements on monthly or periodic statements. Guidance: certification of direct charges is generally acceptable to faculty and auditors and is the primary remaining ‘effort reporting’ in negotiated agreements that eliminate broader effort reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negotiated fixed rate for indirect departmental administration
rubrics_metrics.description: Universities may negotiate a fixed percentage rate for the departmental administration component of indirect costs (e.g., Stanford 19.8%, Yale 18.9%) to eliminate the need for effort reporting to substantiate that component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To obtain agreement, institutions must demonstrate historical stability of the component and may concede a portion of their rate (a discount). Fixed-rate agreements reduce paperwork and audit burdens but typically require periodic validation (every 4–5 years) and may be conditioned on not changing costing policies that affect the pool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional approval/documentation for high federally charged salary fractions
rubrics_metrics.description: Require documented approval by department head or dean when a tenure-line investigator's combined direct salary charges to federal grants exceed a threshold (e.g., 50% general faculty; 80% for medical school faculty).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stanford's agreement requires documented approval for such cases and retention of files for audit. This provides an oversight control while allowing elimination of broader effort reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relief from project-by-project documentation of voluntary cost sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreements may relieve institutions from documenting voluntary cost sharing on a project-by-project basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stanford's pact included such relief. Institutions should negotiate specific language and document any concessions and their accounting treatment to ensure audit defensibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of statistical sampling/interviews to validate effort components
rubrics_metrics.description: When validation data are needed to renew fixed-rate agreements, institutions may use statistical sampling or interviews of a limited number of faculty (agreed with auditors) to estimate faculty effort components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both Stanford and Yale planned to use sampling techniques accepted by auditors as superior to conventional methods. Guidance: develop sampling methodology collaboratively with the cognizant agency and document sampling design, selection, and findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical schools and Medicare-Medicaid requirements remain applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Negotiated relief from A-21 effort reporting does not relieve medical school clinical faculty of Medicare-Medicaid requirements to account for 100% of time spent in patient care and medical education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions operating hospitals must maintain compliance with other federal programs' reporting requirements even when A-21 effort reporting is modified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid creating false categories separating teaching and research
rubrics_metrics.description: Effort reporting systems should not impose artificial separations (false categories) between teaching and research that misrepresent academic work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The workshop warns that false categories could become real over time and disrupt integration of teaching and research. Design reporting rules that recognize intermingling and avoid incentives that push faculty to separate activities unnaturally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize paperwork burden and costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Effort accountability systems should consider the paperwork and administrative costs imposed on institutions and the government and aim to reduce unnecessary burdens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stanford and Yale reported large paperwork savings and reduced audit time. Evaluation of systems should include administrative cost-benefit analysis; where existing systems are efficient and accepted, incentives to change are lower.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit defensibility of effort reporting data
rubrics_metrics.description: Effort reporting data and chosen accountability methods must be defensible to federal auditors; otherwise institutions risk disallowances and damage to public confidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document methodology, historical stability, approximations, certifications, and any negotiated concessions. Be prepared for auditors to challenge distributions; agreements should specify validation/renegotiation processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate reporting for summer compensation for nine-month faculty
rubrics_metrics.description: Faculty with nine-month appointments require a separate form/report for summer compensation periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Yale instructions specify separate reporting for summer pay. Institutions should ensure forms and procedures explicitly address different appointment periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records qualifying as support (payroll/timecards) must meet A-21 requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Where institutions use payroll systems or timecards, those records can qualify as support for payroll and payroll charges provided they meet the documentation requirements set forth in A-21.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that time cards or other payroll records contain the necessary detail and are retained according to policy; provide auditors with clear mapping between payroll records and reported charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional commitment to not change costing policies affecting negotiated pools
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of negotiated fixed-rate agreements, institutions may agree not to change costing policies or procedures that would affect the Indirect Departmental expense component for the duration of the agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Yale's agreement included such a commitment. This stabilizes the base used for negotiation but requires administrative discipline and documentation of any allowed changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic validation/renegotiation of negotiated fixed rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Fixed-rate agreements are time-limited and should be revalidated periodically (e.g., 4–5 years) using agreed statistical or survey methods to ensure the fixed rate remains representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stanford's pact ran five years; Yale's four years. Guidance: plan validation techniques in advance, negotiate validation triggers, and document outcomes to support future negotiations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cognizant agency negotiation and concurrence
rubrics_metrics.description: Negotiation of alternative accountability methods (fixed rates, sampling approaches) requires agreement and concurrence of the cognizant negotiating agency (e.g., DOD/ONR, HHS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agreements with agencies should be memorialized in writing and may be applied retroactively if agreed. Ensure formal concurrence letters are obtained and retained (Yale & HHS example).
